findings.description: `commitsPastPin` now rethrows `RewrittenGitDirError`. `recordMerge` calls it before `appendEvent(db, session.id, 'merge', …)`. So a main `.git` rewritten after the fast-forward lands means the `merge` event is never written, even though the session is already `merged` and the target already holds the sha.
findings.body:
**A `.git` rewritten after the fast-forward drops the `merge` event for a merge that already landed.**

Before this PR, `commitsPastPin` ended in `catch { return 0; }`. Two things changed:
- It now calls `rethrowIfNoUsableRepo(repoPath, error)` ([L1454-L1464](https://github.com/AlexisBalayre/pupitre/blob/8bad0037931130c8af07ea2c26840a16443c2986/src/core/merge-gate.service.ts#L1454-L1464)).
- `resolveCommit` now begins with `assertMainCheckout`.

`recordMerge` calls `commitsPastPin` before `appendEvent`, so a refusal there skips the event. That breaks the promise in `gateAndMerge`'s `finally`: the merge is "recorded even if the teardown threw, since the target already holds the pinned sha".

**How it happens.** ADR 0172's premise is that a session can write `.git`.
1. `fastForward` lands (~L2076) and the session moves to `merged` (~L2081). The session is still alive until `killTmux` (~L2090), and a background child of it can live longer.
2. During that window it plants `.git/commondir` or swaps `.git`.
3. `worktree remove` (~L2092) throws in `safeArgv`. The error is caught and `keptWorktree` is set.
4. `deleteBranchAt` is skipped, so `isDeleted` stays `false`.
5. In the `finally`, `recordMerge` calls `commitsPastPin`, which calls `resolveCommit`, which throws.
6. No `merge` event is written.

**What it costs.**
- `newestMerge` (~L1681) finds nothing. In PR mode, `pinnedPullRequest` then says the session opened no PR, which blocks `land`, ci-wait, fix-round and retire for a session that is already `merged`.
- `regate.service.ts:228` always passes `isDeleted=false`, so a re-gate loses its new merge event the same way.
- Nothing writes the event again later, and no test covers this rethrow.

The refusal should still surface, but after the durable record. Write the event without `leftBehind`, then rethrow.

findings.description: `rethrowIfNoUsableRepo` only spots git's refusal by matching English stderr. Under a translated git and a non-English locale (e.g. `LANG=fr_FR.UTF-8` with git's locale files installed) the match always fails. A `.git` broken after `safeArgv`'s check then reads as "no such ref", which is the outcome this helper exists to stop.

The PR lets `RewrittenGitDirError` through some catches that read a failed git as a negative answer, but not all of them. `isAncestor` still turns it into `false`, and in the gate that becomes a `fresh-base` FAIL. The session is then rejected and re-steered, not refused. The same gap is in `swapBranch`'s catch (L1812-1820) and in `deleteBranchIfHeld` (session-teardown.service.ts:119-125). Each one needs `.git` rewritten between two adjacent spawns, and the fix is the same `rethrowIfNoUsableRepo(repoPath, error)` line in each catch.

`worktreeConfigState`'s catch turns the `RewrittenGitDirError` that `safeArgv` now throws (planted commondir, junk HEAD, unsearchable refs/) into `'unreadable'`. Launch then fails with a `WorktreeConfigError` that tells the operator to run sparse-checkout/config commands and never names the planted file. Fix: rethrow `RewrittenGitDirError` after `rethrowIfKilled(error)`.

`assertMainCheckout(repoPath)` runs inside the conductor's `prepareGraph` envelope. That envelope prints any error as "Could not index …: launching without a code graph", cut to 300 chars, and then launches the conductor anyway. A planted commondir therefore shows up as a truncated no-graph line, with no compromise alarm. The check also runs only when a codegraph binary is installed.

ADR "What remains" says only the symlink and commondir cases are refused for a checkout no `assertMainCheckout` recorded. But `assertGitDirUnplanted` checks HEAD/objects/refs on every spawn, so the bare-fallback and unusable-.git cases are refused there too. The real gaps are a gitfile swap, a missing .git, and a decoy directory.

Call-site comments restate `assertMainCheckout`'s JSDoc (a .git dir of its own, no commondir, gitfile/symlink, safeArgv holds the path). They do this here and at conductor.service.ts:152-153, which also wrongly puts a gitfile/symlink "in" .git. general.md §Comments says to keep only the ordering WHY, e.g. "before any ref read, and again under the lock (decision 172)".

The HEAD/objects/refs pre-check (`VALID_HEAD`, `searchableDir`) copies git's `is_git_directory` rules. Explicit `--git-dir` naming plus `safe.bareRepository=explicit` already stop the bare fallback, and `rethrowIfNoUsableRepo` already refuses git's "not a git repository". Removing the pre-check would cut about 35 lines and one regex to keep in step with git, at the cost of a less specific message.

The second `assertMainCheckout` under the lock repeats the check that the next spawn (via `safeArgv`) and `resolveCommit` make anyway, since L1074 has already recorded the path. It could be dropped, together with its "and again under the lock" justification.

docs/adr/README.md:15 numbers a new ADR as the highest on origin/main plus one, which gives 0168 at this merge base, but this ADR is 0172. Renumber unless 0168-0171 are reserved on other branches. The source comments cite "decision 172" too.
